components.name: Windows Search
components.description: Indexes local content and supplies Windows search experiences.
components.reason: A dedicated DAW may not need indexing or system search.
components.consequences: Search experiences and indexed lookup can stop working.

components.name: Bing Search
components.description: Adds web suggestions to Windows search.
components.reason: Web results are unnecessary on an offline-focused DAW.
components.consequences: Windows search no longer offers Bing suggestions.

components.name: Widgets and Client.WebExperience
components.description: Provides the Widgets board and Windows Web Experience package.
components.reason: Widgets add background and consumer content not needed for audio work.
components.consequences: Widgets and features hosted by WebExperience become unavailable.

components.name: Copilot
components.description: Provides Microsoft's Copilot application and Windows integration.
components.reason: The Lean DAW profile does not use assistant integration.
components.consequences: Copilot entry points and the provisioned app are unavailable.

components.name: Feedback Hub
components.description: Collects and submits Windows feedback and diagnostics.
components.reason: Feedback submission is not required on the reference workstation.
components.consequences: The Feedback Hub application is unavailable.

components.name: Microsoft Defender
components.description: Provides built-in antimalware, drivers, services, and security integration.
components.reason: The reference profile deliberately delegates endpoint protection elsewhere.
components.consequences: Removing Defender materially reduces built-in protection and may affect servicing integrations.

components.name: SmartScreen
components.description: Checks downloaded files and applications against reputation services.
components.reason: The Lean DAW profile opts out of reputation checks.
components.consequences: Windows provides fewer warnings for unknown or malicious downloads.

components.name: User Account Control
components.description: Separates standard and elevated administrative operations.
components.reason: The Lean DAW default requests full UAC disable for unattended local operation.
components.consequences: Disabling EnableLUA weakens security and can break modern applications.

components.name: Windows AI (Client.CoreAI and Client.AIX)
components.description: Supplies Windows AI platform components including Client.CoreAI and Client.AIX.
components.reason: The reference DAW does not require Windows AI functionality.
components.consequences: Windows AI features may fail and package removal can affect future upgrades.

components.name: OneDrive
components.description: Provides Microsoft cloud file synchronization and shell integration.
components.reason: Cloud file synchronization is outside the Lean DAW workflow.
components.consequences: OneDrive sync and its Explorer integration are unavailable.

components.name: Xbox, Game Bar, and Game DVR
components.description: Provides Xbox applications, overlays, recording, Game Bar, and Game DVR.
components.reason: Gaming overlays and capture are unnecessary for the target DAW.
components.consequences: Xbox services, Game Bar, and Windows game capture are unavailable.

components.name: Selected consumer AppX packages
components.description: Groups the explicitly selected news, weather, solitaire, and Clipchamp provisioned applications.
components.reason: These consumer applications are not part of the reference workstation workflow.
components.consequences: The selected provisioned applications are absent for new users.

components.name: Telemetry and consumer content
components.description: Controls selected diagnostic telemetry tasks and promoted consumer content.
components.reason: The Lean DAW minimizes nonessential diagnostics and content suggestions.
components.consequences: Some diagnostic data and personalized content are disabled while WER remains protected separately.

components.name: NFS client
components.description: Provides Windows client support and administration tools for Network File System shares.
components.reason: NFS must remain available for development and storage workflows.
components.consequences: Protection prevents broad feature rules from removing NFS payloads.

components.name: Modern Start menu and File Explorer
components.description: Provides the supported modern Start and Explorer shell experiences.
components.reason: The reference image must retain a functional Windows shell.
components.consequences: Removal can leave Windows without a usable Start menu or shell.

components.name: Client.CBS
components.description: Supplies core client shell and component-based servicing integration.
components.reason: Modern shell and servicing compatibility depend on Client.CBS.
components.consequences: Removal can break shell experiences and Windows servicing.

components.name: Microsoft Store infrastructure
components.description: Provides Store package acquisition, licensing, and installation infrastructure.
components.reason: Store and packaged application servicing must remain available.
components.consequences: Removal can prevent Store and MSIX application installation or updates.

components.name: App Installer and WinGet
components.description: Provides App Installer and the WinGet package manager client.
components.reason: Application installation and developer setup depend on WinGet.
components.consequences: Removal eliminates WinGet and common MSIX installation paths.

components.name: Windows Terminal
components.description: Provides the modern terminal host for shells and developer tools.
components.reason: The developer-capable reference image retains Windows Terminal.
components.consequences: Removal loses the supported modern terminal application.

components.name: WebView2
components.description: Hosts web content inside Windows desktop applications.
components.reason: Many retained desktop and developer applications require WebView2.
components.consequences: Removal can break applications that embed web interfaces.

components.name: Windows App Runtime
components.description: Provides runtime libraries for modern Windows desktop applications.
components.reason: App Installer, Terminal, and other retained apps depend on this runtime.
components.consequences: Removal can prevent Windows App SDK applications from launching.

components.name: UI.Xaml
components.description: Provides XAML framework packages used by modern Windows applications.
components.reason: Retained packaged applications require UI.Xaml frameworks.
components.consequences: Removal can stop dependent applications from starting.

components.name: VCLibs runtime frameworks
components.description: Provides Visual C++ runtime frameworks for packaged applications.
components.reason: App Installer, Terminal, and other retained applications require VCLibs.
components.consequences: Removal can prevent dependent applications from launching.

components.name: Windows Subsystem for Linux
components.description: Provides Windows Subsystem for Linux payloads and integration.
components.reason: The developer profile must be able to enable WSL later.
components.consequences: Removal prevents WSL installation or use without restoring payloads.

components.name: VirtualMachinePlatform
components.description: Provides virtualization components used by WSL2 and virtualized workloads.
components.reason: The reference image retains the ability to enable WSL2 and related tooling.
components.consequences: Removal prevents dependent virtualization features from being enabled.

components.name: Hyper-V payloads
components.description: Provides Hyper-V optional-feature payloads without requiring the hypervisor to be enabled.
components.reason: Keeping dormant payloads preserves future virtualization capability.
components.consequences: Removal prevents Hyper-V features from being enabled without source media.

components.name: Windows Error Reporting
components.description: Captures application and system failure reports and dump information.
components.reason: Crash diagnostics are valuable for DAW and plugin troubleshooting.
components.consequences: Removal makes failures harder to diagnose and can suppress crash reporting.

components.name: Program and App Compatibility
components.description: Supplies application compatibility databases, shims, and the Program Compatibility Assistant.
components.reason: Older DAW software and plugins may require compatibility infrastructure.
components.consequences: Removal can break installers or applications that rely on compatibility shims.

components.name: SysMain and Prefetch
components.description: Optimizes application launch using usage history and prefetch data.
components.reason: The project retains these components until measurements justify changing them.
components.consequences: Disabling them can worsen launch performance on some systems.

components.name: Windows feature-delivery infrastructure
components.description: Coordinates Windows feature delivery and update orchestration.
components.reason: Normal feature delivery must remain serviceable.
components.consequences: Removal can block feature updates and optional content delivery.

components.name: FeatureConfig and OneSettings
components.description: Provides Windows feature configuration and OneSettings infrastructure.
components.reason: Retaining feature configuration reduces upgrade and feature-delivery breakage.
components.consequences: Removal can break managed feature state and future Windows changes.

components.name: CPU security mitigations
components.description: Controls operating-system mitigations for speculative execution vulnerabilities.
components.reason: No established DAW benefit justifies disabling CPU security mitigations by default.
components.consequences: Disabling mitigations exposes known CPU vulnerability classes.

components.name: Windows servicing tasks
components.description: Runs scheduled component servicing and maintenance operations.
components.reason: Servicing tasks are required for a maintainable Windows installation.
components.consequences: Removal can prevent maintenance and component repair.

components.name: WinSxS component store
components.description: Stores component payloads and metadata used by Windows servicing and repair.
components.reason: The component store must remain intact and is never manually deleted.
components.consequences: Damage can make Windows unserviceable or unbootable.

components.name: Windows rollback state
components.description: Retains superseded component state needed to uninstall updates when supported.
components.reason: Normal reversible cleanup must preserve update rollback state.
components.consequences: Discarding rollback state makes installed updates permanently non-removable.

components.name: Windows Update
components.description: Scans, downloads, and installs Windows updates and servicing fixes.
components.reason: The reference image must remain updateable and supported.
components.consequences: Removal prevents normal security and quality updates.

components.name: Reversible component cleanup
components.description: Provides supported component-store cleanup without ResetBase.
components.reason: Cleanup remains supported while update rollback data is preserved.
components.consequences: Replacing it with irreversible cleanup can prevent update uninstall.
